newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador considering Colombian electricity imports.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador considering Colombian electricity imports.

text.p: Ecuador is considering relieving its energy deficit by plugging into neighboring Colombia's electricity grid, Energy and Mines Minister Raul Baca said Wednesday.
"We are sketching plans for the first (power) lines, which would naturally at first reach the northern part of the country," Baca told reporters.

"But the fundamental intention is to expand this agreement aiming to build a power line to Quito which can be connected up and provide energy so that we are not affected by power cuts next year," he said.
The power line would also allow electricity exports to Colombia in years when Ecuador has a power surplus, Baca said.
The government fears the country's electricity shortage is putting the breaks on economic growth, but Baca said that projects now planned should produce an extra 1,000 MW by 1999.

Seventy percent of the electricity now available to the Andean nation of 12 million people is generated by one power plant, and Ecuadoreans have faced tough electricity rationing over the past two years.
Private analysts estimate Ecuador has lost $470 million due to power shortages since 1995.
